perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s subjective perspective, he has access to:

- He is a project manager and feels frustrated/anxious because his project is not progressing well; he believes his team lacks motivation.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a friend and police officer whom he relies on for advice. He arranges and attends a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur.
- In that meeting, Harold tells Arthur his team seems unmotivated and it is affecting progress. He hears Arthur suggest understanding each team member’s individual motivations and having one-on-one conversations. Harold admits he had focused on goals/deadlines, agrees to try Arthur’s advice, and feels hopeful.
- Afterward, Harold feels hopeful/relieved and believes Arthur’s advice will help. He tells the team he wants one-on-one chats about what motivates them. He hears Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they are open to it. He schedules time with each and asks them to work together for the project’s success.
- Later, Harold observes the team still is not responding well. He feels disappointed and worried, then tells Arthur the suggestions did not work. He hears Arthur say there may be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper. Harold decides to set up another round of meetings.
- He then feels determined and focused, believes underlying issues may exist, and asks team members about concerns/problems. He hears Team Member 1 report tension among a few members affecting work, and Team Member 2 report feeling overwhelmed by workload and stressed. Harold says he will look into resolving conflicts and see about redistributing tasks, emphasizing their well-being.
- Finally, Harold feels optimistic and empowered, believes addressing individual concerns will improve performance, and tells the team he will create a more supportive/open environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. He hears Team Member 1 say that sounds great and Team Member 2 agree that concerns are being addressed. He says their input and well-being are crucial and urges working together for success.

He does not have access to the private thoughts or motives of Arthur or the team members beyond what they said or what he observed, nor to narrator-only characterizations.
